top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock is a distinct, mechanism-level invention (equal light shifts for both clock levels allow thousands of neutral atoms to be interrogated without Stark, Doppler or recoil penalties) and its 10^-18 performance has been reproduced across several laboratories. It is separable from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes if the citation is written around the lattice concept. The Katori and Ye attribution is the cleanest available, so I prefer awarding P001 to no award, despite the lack of a delivered fundamental-physics result and the omitted hands-on contributors.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; Gothenburg proximity to Chalmers colleagues only, no tie to Katori or Ye
